name: Weekly CISplatin plus concurrent radiation (alternative schedule)
disease: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

biomarkers.note: For p16-positive (HPV-associated) oropharyngeal cancer, p16/HPV status is prognostic but NOT a dose gate. Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 concurrent with accelerated RT was the chemoradiation arm carried forward in HN002 for p16-positive oropharyngeal cancer (DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 23, line 62073).

lineOfTherapy: alternative concurrent chemoradiation schedule where high-dose every-3-week cisplatin is not preferred; definitive or postoperative; not line-scoped

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: locoregionally advanced SCCHN treated with concurrent radiation where a weekly low-dose cisplatin schedule is chosen as an alternative to high-dose every-3-week cisplatin
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
eligibilityCriteria.locator: Discussion lines 8782, 8875, 8886, 9816 (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 may be substituted); algorithm line 6171 (Weekly Cisplatin 40 mg/m2)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: weekly cisplatin doses below 40 mg/m2 should not be used in this setting
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
eligibilityCriteria.locator: Discussion line 8783 (weekly doses of cisplatin of less than 40 mg/m2 should not be utilized)

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
provenance.locator: Algorithm line 6171 (Weekly Cisplatin 40 mg/m2); Discussion lines 8782 (40 mg/m2/week may be substituted), 9816 (40 mg/m2/week or 100 mg/m2 every 21 days)

drugs.notes: Source: cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV weekly concurrent with radiation. Corroborated DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 23, lines 62066 to 62068 (NRG HN009) and 62073 (HN002): concurrent weekly cisplatin 40 mg per m2 every 1 week. Number of weekly doses runs with the radiation course and is not fixed by the cited source (see verifyFields). Doses below 40 mg/m2/week are not recommended (NCCN Discussion line 8783). ISMP tall-man. No lifetime cumulative cap for cisplatin; monitor nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, neuropathy; hydrate with each dose.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 (below the 50 mg/m2 high-emetic-risk threshold): moderate-to-high emetic risk; provide prophylaxis. Confirm exact institutional tier.

premedications.name: Hydration
premedications.notes: IV hydration with each weekly dose to reduce nephrotoxicity.

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: cisplatin-containing; provide prophylaxis per emetogenicity. Confirm exact institutional/guideline tier.
Nephroprotection: IV hydration and electrolyte (Mg, K) repletion with each weekly dose.

monitoring: Renal function (creatinine/GFR) and electrolytes (Mg, K, Na) before each weekly dose - cisplatin nephrotoxicity

doseModificationRules.condition: rising creatinine / falling GFR, ototoxicity, or grade 2+ neuropathy
doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Weekly doses below 40 mg/m2 are not recommended (NCCN Discussion line 8783); consider hold or switch rather than reducing below the floor. Physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Chapter 23, lines 62066 to 62068 (NRG HN009) and 62073 (HN002): concurrent weekly cisplatin 40 mg per m2

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for weekly CISplatin concurrent with radiation, the alternative low-dose schedule to high-dose every-3-week cisplatin. Setting: definitive or postoperative concurrent chemoradiation. Sites served (squamous histology): oral cavity (#32), tongue (#33), lip (#34), oropharyngeal (#35), HPV-positive oropharyngeal (#36, p16/HPV prognostic only, not a dose gate), hypopharyngeal (#38), laryngeal (#39), sinonasal (#41); nasopharyngeal (#37) is covered by the dedicated NPC protocols and salivary (#40) is not covered. Dose fully grounded: CISplatin 40 mg/m2 IV weekly (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) 2.2026 algorithm line 6171 and Discussion lines 8782/9816; DeVita 12th ed. Chapter 23 lines 62066 to 62068 (NRG HN009) and 62073 (HN002)). The number of weekly cycles runs with the radiation course and is not fixed by the cited source, so regimen.cycles is set to VERIFY. A dose floor is enforced: weekly doses below 40 mg/m2 are not recommended (NCCN Discussion line 8783). ISMP tall-man applied. Cisplatin has NO lifetime cumulative cap; nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and neuropathy monitoring plus hydration are specified. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
